title: END EXERCISE — Glass House

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The exercise concludes. All systems are restored to baseline. The emergency alert lights on the control board fade to green. The AOC returns to normal operations status.
finalState: The rogue Raspberry Pi device has been isolated and removed from the network.
The log gap on the core switch has been analyzed and attributed to a covert data exfiltration window.
The criminal syndicate has been reported to CISA and FBI Cyber Division; no further breaches are detected.
Jordan Kelley has been placed on administrative leave pending a full investigation.
The airport's PCI-DSS compliance status is under review by an external auditor.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will take ten minutes, then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up / 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: What actions demonstrated strong leadership under pressure, and why?
Where did trust in the IT manager compromise incident response, and how could that have been prevented?
How would you modify your access control policies to prevent a single point of failure like this in the future?
What changes would you recommend to the airport’s cyber hygiene and insider threat monitoring program?
How should the airport balance rapid response to technical alerts with verification and two-person integrity checks?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect all player action logs and evaluator sheets. Begin hot wash within 10 minutes. Remind facilitators to close the loop on the AAR process via formal Plan Amendment.
